Some weeks test your roster construction. Others test your decision-making. Week 7 tested whether anyone in this league can read.

---

## New Vertical Threats 167.6 def. Maia's Monstrous Team 72.62
**Subtitle: When Your Opponent Forgets Football Exists**

New Vertical Threats put up 167.6 points—54.1 above projection—while starting a QB who scored 6.6. That's not a typo. Tua Tagovailoa gave them replacement-level production and they still won by 94.98 points because Rico Dowdle (33.9), Drake London (31.8), and Josh Jacobs (32.0) decided violence was the answer. Meanwhile, Caleb Williams sat on the bench with 19.9 points, proving that even when you make the wrong decision, sometimes the universe just shrugs and gives you the win anyway.

Maia's Monstrous Team scored 72.62 points. In a 12-team league. In 2024. They benched DK Metcalf's 19.5 points and fielded a roster so thin it looked like a startup's org chart after Series A funding fell through. Jared Goff (16.8) was their second-highest scorer. Their running backs combined for less than some kickers. This wasn't a football team—it was a cry for help formatted as a lineup card.

What they'll tell themselves: "We're strategically managing our expectations to align with realistic outcome-based scenarios."

Jaxon Smith-Njigba (30.2) and Cameron Dicker (17.0) carried the load while Baker Mayfield (19.6) did his best Baker Mayfield impression—just good enough to not screw it up.

Beacon is now 0-6, which feels less like bad luck and more like a lifestyle choice. They started Drake Maye (27.2) at QB—actual pattern recognition!—and got quality outings from their Rams D/ST (16.0) and Michael Mayer (16.0). Then J.K. Dobbins scored 4.0 points and reminded everyone why starting Chargers running backs requires either courage or a concussion protocol waiver. Lost by 22.1 despite doing several things right, which is the most Beacon outcome imaginable.

What they'll tell themselves: "Moral victories are just regular victories with better branding."

---

## Purdy Boys 88.32 def. Hot Chubb Time Machine 79.34
**Subtitle: A 52-Point Projection Miss Meets a 13-Point One**

Hot Chubb Time Machine projected 131.5 points and scored 79.34. That's not a miss—that's a different sport. Puka Nacua (4.8 points on a 22.8 projection) apparently forgot he plays football for a living, and Quinshon Judkins (3.6 on 13.8 projected) decided to join him in witness protection. They left Kayshon Boutte's 26.3 points on the bench because why would you start a player who might actually help? Jonathan Taylor (23.7) and Dak Prescott (22.3) played well, but watching your team underperform by 52.2 points is like ordering a pizza and getting a photo of a pizza instead.

Purdy Boys won despite Courtland Sutton scoring 2.7 points on a 13.3 projection, which takes genuine skill.
